items.title: Bill Dobbins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: two of the people that Ray talked to, to see if they knew of anybody that they thought would be good for this job were this music critic, Ted Price, and he just happened to have as a guest soloist with the Eastman Jazz Ensemble right then, Clark Terry. ctx.x: And I think it was about ’71, maybe ’72, no I think it was ’71, that Chuck Mangione, he had a really big commercial success with this record that he did with the Rochester Philharmonic called “Friends and Love.” And he had been teaching here as an instructor at the time that Ray came up from Radio City in New York and decided to move to Rochester and start a — well mostly a jazz writing curriculum. Chuck had been doing improvisation and they had a big band here, and so Ray came to do a whole sequence of writing…

The planets aligned for you. That’s interesting because now I was speculating, if you were to go on and do something else or retire or whatever, I think there’d be a lot of applicants for your position.
